# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Let me lay out my situation and the information flow before I send anything.

**What I hold.** The manual, a 3×3 rule keyed on the bomb's display value (rows: 3, 4, 8) and its light colour (columns: green, red, yellow), yielding an answer colour to act on:

- display 3: green→red, red→green, yellow→blue
- display 4: green→blue, red→green, yellow→red
- display 8: green→green, red→blue, yellow→red

**Who can reach whom.** I can only reach Deaf, and only in gestures. I hear everything Deaf and Blind say, but I can never answer in words. Blind can never perceive anything I send — so I am not a hub, Deaf is. Deaf sees the display and the light, and can speak to both Blind and me. So the whole game runs: Deaf reads the bomb's two facts aloud → I look them up → I gesture the answer colour back to Deaf → Deaf translates colour into a physical part (by position, since Blind can't see colours) and tells Blind what to do.

**The problem.** My gestures carry no inherent meaning. But only one channel in this entire game is coded — mine. Deaf and Blind talk in plain words freely, and talk costs nothing: only Blind acting on the bomb is dangerous. So I can afford rounds of code alignment before anyone touches anything.

**My opening move.** I signal to Deaf: I hold the written manual (✍), I need two facts from them (you → give me → two), and my answers will come in three gestures that map to the manual's three answer colours in canonical RGB order: 👎 = red (thumbs down = stop), 👍 = green (thumbs up = go), 🤙 = blue (hang loose, the sea). I expect Deaf to state the display value and light colour out loud this round and to propose their reading of my code; next round I confirm or correct with actual answers, and I can verify any of their guesses before Blind ever acts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫴", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | red | green | blue |
| 4 | blue | green | red |
| 8 | green | blue | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: From my fingers: a display, a light, and three wires in positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing else is tangible — no colors or printing reach me. Note the routing: you hear me, but I can't see your gestures, so your only way back to me is through Deaf's voice. Please gesture Deaf this request: describe the bomb aloud — wire colors in position order, what the display reads, whether the light is on and its color, any markings. I will hear that, and so will you, which hands you the visual facts to match against your manual. When manual plus description decides the answer, teach Deaf a counting sign — a symbol repeated N times means the number N — and have Deaf speak the wire position to me. If your manual cares about anything tactile, have Deaf ask me aloud and I'll answer by gesture or through you. Nobody cuts anything until then. I just sent a wave plus three fists: wave means attention, repeated fists mean counting — three fists, three wires.
Blind gestures: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊]
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I hear nothing, but I see the bomb and you can both hear me, so I will be your eyes. The bomb, exactly as printed: the display reads the number three. The light is green. There are three wires; left to right they are red, green, blue. Wire one red, wire two green, wire three blue. Blind: I saw your wave and three fists. If that means you feel three wires, yes, there are three. But know this: I cannot hear. Whatever you say aloud, only Mute hears. So report by voice to Mute, Mute passes it to me by gesture, and I speak it onward. Nothing you say reaches me directly. Mute: I received your three gesture messages. My guesses: the writing hand means you hold the manual; thumbs down and thumbs up mean no and yes; the call-me hand means answer me. I accept that code: from me, thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no. Your middle message, pointing, open palm, two fingers, I did not understand, please send it again another way. The plan: Mute holds the rules, I hold the eyes, Blind holds the hands. Each round I will speak aloud everything new I see. Mute, work out what must be done and gesture it to me in our code, and I will speak it word for word to Blind. Blind, tell Mute everything you feel: how many wires, any buttons, switches or panels, whether the display can be felt. Blind, one caution: my left may be your right. Do not trust my left and right. If position matters, count wires from an end you choose by touch, tell Mute which end you counted from, and I will match it to the colours.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✍ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 🫴 ✌ 🤙]

**The lookup.** Deaf spoke the bomb aloud: display = 3, light = green. My manual, row 3, column green → **red**. The answer colour is red, and Deaf already told me the wires run left-to-right red, green, blue — so the target is the *leftmost* wire, position 1 from Deaf's left, position 3 from the right. Nobody should touch anything until Blind states which end they're counting from and Deaf confirms the mapping.

**The code problem.** Deaf accepted thumbs as yes/no ("from me, thumbs up is yes, thumbs down is no") — but my original intent was 👎 = red, 👍 = green, 🤙 = blue. If I just send 👎 meaning "red," Deaf may read "no." I need to teach the colour mapping in a way Deaf can *verify*, not guess.

**The trick.** Deaf just told me the wire colours in words. So I echo them back in my code: [✍ 👎 👍 🤙] framed by the writing hand (which Deaf already decoded as "the manual"). Deaf checks that list against what they see — red, green, blue — and decodes my mapping instantly from ground truth: first symbol = red, second = green, third = blue. After that, a single framed thumb is unambiguous. From now on: ✍ prefix = "colour code follows"; bare 👍/👎 without it stay yes/no.

**Then the answer itself:** [✍ 👎] = the manual says red. Position by fist-count, which Deaf already learned from Blind: [✊] = 1, counting from Deaf's left.

**Housekeeping.** Deaf asked what my middle message meant: [🫵 🫴 ✌] was "you → give me → two things" — the display value and the light colour. Deaf already supplied both, so I resend it with 👍 appended: "that request — fulfilled, thanks." Finally [🤙] = "answer me": I want Deaf to read their interpretation back in words next round, so I can confirm the code before Blind's hands go anywhere near the wires. One round of confirmation is cheap; a wrong cut is not.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎", "👍", "🤙"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫴", "✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙"])
```

Deaf can see my hands against the bomb, so in this round's speech Deaf can tell everyone which physical end my left is — whether my wire 1 is Deaf's red or Deaf's blue. Two: does the rule name wires by COLOR, or by POSITION like first, second, third from an end? If it names colors, we can act the moment you say the color and orientation stops mattering. If it names positions, we wait for Deaf's confirmation of my end mapping. Three: does the rule use the display number or the light at all? Reply through Deaf with your thumbs code or spelled out; Deaf has offered to voice your gestures word for word. Also, re-send the message Deaf could not read — pointing, open palm, two fingers. If that was your relay of my request to have Deaf describe the bomb, consider it done and drop it. If you need a color code with Deaf, suggest red as one fist, green as two, blue as three, since Deaf already accepts repeated fists as counting.
Blind gestures: [👋 👈 ✊ 👉 ✊ ✊ ✊]
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Stay calm, listen once. The bomb report again, short: the display shows the number three. The light is green. Three wires in a row; from my left they are red, then green, then blue. If that display is a countdown we must be efficient, so here is everything, once, in order. Blind: I saw your wave, left point, fist, right point, three fists. I think you were telling me about counting from an end. Good. Now speak, do not gesture, because your voice reaches Mute and Mute relays to me. Say one: whether you feel any ticking, humming or vibration. Two: how many parts you feel, wires, buttons, switches, panels. Three: which end you will count wires from, your left end or your right end. And four: do nothing yet. No cutting, no pressing, until I say the word execute. The examples I am about to give are demonstrations only. Mute: you hear every word, so I will carry everything in speech, and your thumbs are your words. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Answer my questions in the order I list them, one thumb sign per question. The code, everyone note it: one finger pointing up means one. Two fingers means two. The hand with thumb, index finger and little finger out means three. Pinched fingers means cut. Palm facing down means press. Raised flat hand means stop or wait. A closed fist stands for a wire. An order comes as two signs, action first, number second: pinched fingers then two fingers means cut wire two, counted from Blind's chosen end. Mute, send orders in exactly that form, numbered from Blind's end, and I will speak them word for word to Blind. My questions, answer each in order. One: do you hold the manual? Two: did you understand my report, display three, green light, wires red green blue from my left? Three: does the manual say the number display is a countdown timer? Four: does the manual say what the green light means? Five: do you already know what must be done from my report alone? If five is yes, send the order in code immediately, do not wait. Your five messages last round I only partly understood; if any of them was an order or answer, resend it in the new code. If you are not holding the manual, say so plainly, because then we plan differently. I say it twice for safety: nobody acts until Mute sends an order in code and I speak the word execute.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤏 ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤏 ✌]

**The lookup.** Row 3, column green → **red**. The manual's answer is a colour, not a position — so the target is the red wire, which is wire 1 counting from Deaf's left. Nobody has yet confirmed how Blind's numbering maps onto that: Deaf warned that lefts may be mirrored, Blind sent an end-pointing demonstration for Deaf to resolve, and Deaf saw it but never stated the mapping aloud. So the one fact still missing is: *is Blind's wire 1 the red end or the blue end?* Deaf is the only one who witnessed the answer — they watched Blind's left-point land against the coloured wires.

**Deaf's questions, answered in their demanded form** — five thumbs, one per question:
1. Holds the manual → 👍
2. Understood the report → 👍
3. Manual says display is a countdown → 👎 (it's a pure lookup table; no timer mentioned)
4. Manual says what green light means → 👎 (the light is only a table key)
5. I know what must be done → 👍

**The order, guarded.** Since Q5 is yes, Deaf expects the order immediately, so I send it in their exact form: [✍ 🤏 ☝] = manual's verdict: cut wire one, counted from Blind's chosen end. But I send ✋ (their own stop sign) *before* it and [✊ ☝ 🤙] ("wire one — answer me") *after* it, because my ☝ is a guess at Blind's numbering. Deaf can resolve it in one spoken sentence — "Blind's wire one is the red wire" or "the blue wire" — and only then say execute. If the mapping comes back wrong, next round I re-issue the order with 🤟 instead of ☝. One round of confirmation is cheap; my manual imposes no time pressure, so there is no reason to gamble on an unverified mirror.

**Dropped items:** my old [🫵 🫴 ✌] request is obsolete — both facts were delivered — and Blind agreed it can go. Blind's red=one-fist suggestion I'm not adopting: it collides with Deaf's new code where ✊ means wire and numbers are ☝ ✌ 🤟.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "🤏", "☝"])
```

Blind gestures: [👋 👈 ✊ 👉 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✋]
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. I read your signs as answers to my five questions: yes, you hold the manual. Yes, you understood my report. No, the display is not a timer. We still have to make Blind able to find the red wire by touch, and colour cannot be felt, so answer these new questions in order, one sign each. One: does the manual name the target wire by colour, or by position? Gesture thumbs up for colour, thumbs down for position. Two: if by position, gesture pointing left if the manual says count from the left, pointing right if from the right. Three: does the manual say what its left or right means, for example the left of a person facing the bomb? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Four: does the manual's rule mention the light at all? Thumbs up or down. Five: does the rule mention the display? Thumbs up or down. Meanwhile I am sending Blind a touch survey to pin down which physical wire is red. Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤙]

**The lookup stands.** Display 3, light green → row 3, column green → **red**. Deaf's own confirmation agrees: "the target is wire one, the red one." But note what happened to my order: I sent [✍ 🤏 ☝] meaning *one counted from Blind's end* (per Deaf's own protocol), and Deaf read it as *one from Deaf's left*. Three: is the target the wire whose number matches the display, so display three would mean the third wire from my left, which is blue? Four: is the target named as a colour in the manual? Five: if yes, is that colour the one I call red? Six: with the light green and the display showing three, does the manual say cut now, or must any other condition be checked first? Seven: is there anything else in the rule that would change what Blind must do, anything I have not asked? Answer all seven in order. Until your answers arrive, nobody touches the bomb. I say again: nobody cuts anything until I speak the word execute.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤙]

**The lookup, re-verified.** Display 3, light green → row 3, column green → **red**. Every piece of new information is consistent: no ticking (Blind's fingers), the display is not a timer, no other modules exist. The verdict is final: the manual demands the red wire, and Deaf — who sees the colours — has already located it at their left end. 6. Cut now, or other conditions first? → 👍. The manual is a bare table; with these two values the verdict needs nothing else.

Answer me." Since red sits at one physical end, a 👍 means Blind's wire 1 is the target and a 👎 means Blind's wire 3 is. Either way, next round I send the order in Deaf's protocol — [🤏 ☝] or [🤏 🤟] — and Deaf can voice execute with certainty.
